feedback.details: Authorization and file validation can be performed in either order or in parallel; neither is a prerequisite for the other. Publication is the common gate that waits until both have passed.

messages.text: Local queue fields can be modified and may outlive sign-out or permission changes, so identity and record access must be checked at replay.
A file that has not passed quarantine validation must not become available before the scan and type checks finish.
Publishing before checking current record permission can expose an upload to an unauthorized user or attach it to the wrong record.

options.text: At replay, reauthorize the current user for the intended record and validate the queued image in quarantine; publish only after both checks pass.
Trust the queued owner and record identifiers because the original device created the upload before it went offline.
Publish the queued file immediately and scan it afterward so the inspection is available while validation runs.
Validate the file first and publish it, then check whether the current user may attach it to the protected record.

prompt: An offline inspection app queues image uploads locally and replays them when connectivity returns. Which replay policy prevents a modified queue item or file from being published without both required checks?
